statement: States what should centralize is Authority/Identity/Governance/Evidence/Cross-context relationships/High-risk authorization, not all execution — preserving the edge architecture's fast-feedback strength (local: fast feedback, agent integration, working memory, source code, tests, developer tooling; central: authority, governance, knowledge, evidence, assurance, authorization, graph); identifies the major current weakness as 'agent context can be assembled from heterogeneous sources without a universal authority model' — exactly what the Context Service should solve, requiring every high-value context item to carry Source/Authority/Validity/Evidence and a six-value status (AUTHORITATIVE/VERIFIED/OBSERVED/DERIVED/LOCAL/UNKNOWN).

anchor: R1 Authority fragmentation ... R8 Temporal ambiguity. R1>R2>R4>R6>R3>R5>R8>R7.
statement: Defines an eight-item architecture risk register (R1 Authority fragmentation, R2 Relationship implicitness, R3 Agent-memory contamination, R4 Evidence fragmentation, R5 Verification isolation, R6 Action traceability gaps, R7 Projection ambiguity, R8 Temporal ambiguity) with a preliminary priority ordering R1>R2>R4>R6>R3>R5>R8>R7, to be validated against implementation evidence and enterprise risk requirements.

anchor: One semantic authority per concept. Every material relationship must be explicit and addressable. Every material engineering action must be traceable to context, authorization, and evidence. Agent memory is contextual unless explicitly promoted. Deterministic verification outranks probabilistic inference where mechanically verifiable. Derived projections must not become competing sources of truth.
statement: States six first target-architecture principles derived from the archaeology, consolidating prior invariants (source-of-truth, explicit relationships, action traceability, memory-promotion, deterministic-precedence, projection-non-authority) into a single archaeology-derived list.

anchor: Existing KnowledgeOS/EKS + Semantic Formalization + Authority Model + Evidence Integration + Assurance Graph.
statement: Step 142 verdict: rejects 'current platform -> completely new architecture' in favor of an evolutionary model (existing platform plus semantic formalization, authority model, evidence integration, and assurance graph).

anchor: KEEP, STRENGTHEN, FORMALIZE, CONNECT, CONSTRAIN, INTRODUCE, RETIRE.
statement: Opens Step 143 (Current -> Target Architecture Delta): defines seven delta-transformation categories to classify every capability, producing 'what KnowledgeOS actually needs to build' rather than another abstract architecture, and previews Step 144's KnowledgeOS Evolution Roadmap (Current Platform -> Target Architecture) with explicit work packages and sequencing.

anchor: KEEP, STRENGTHEN, FORMALIZE, CONNECT, CONSTRAIN, INTRODUCE, RETIRE.
statement: Restates the seven delta transformation types and presents the master delta map across 19 architecture areas (repository agent integration KEEP+CONSTRAIN; .claude/.codex CONSTRAIN; AGENTS.md KEEP+FORMALIZE; agent memory CONSTRAIN; governance artifacts/architecture knowledge FORMALIZE; registry STRENGTHEN; deterministic checks CONNECT+FORMALIZE; session logging CONNECT; evidence FORMALIZE+CONNECT; verification/findings FORMALIZE; cross-context relationships INTRODUCE; governed context FORMALIZE+CONNECT; authorization STRENGTHEN; external systems CONSTRAIN; auditability CONNECT; temporal knowledge FORMALIZE) — the core transformation map, with the transformation framed as Existing mechanisms -> Explicit semantic contracts -> Governed engineering system.

anchor: KOS-ARCH-001: Agent-local instructions may reference authoritative knowledge but must not redefine it.
statement: Work Package 1-2 (Preserve the Agent Edge / Formalize the Pointer Layer): KEEP repository-local agent integration (.claude/, .codex/, AGENTS.md, local tooling, fast feedback) without centralizing it, establishing AGENTS.md's precise responsibility ('how does an agent enter and operate' not 'what is the authoritative architecture') and formalizing the pointer-layer rule as KOS-ARCH-001, applying equally to Claude and Codex.

anchor: Knowledge Object schema; AuthorityType = f(Context, ClaimType) — not AUTHORITATIVE > EVERYTHING.
statement: Work Package 3 (Establish Knowledge Authority), one of the highest-priority changes: a Knowledge Object schema (identity, type, source, authority, status, validity, provenance, relationships) and a seven-level authority classification (AUTHORITATIVE, VERIFIED, OBSERVED, DERIVED, PROPOSED, LOCAL, UNKNOWN) explicitly not a linear ranking — corrects a simplistic 'AUTHORITATIVE > everything' view with AuthorityType=f(Context,ClaimType), e.g. Kubernetes authoritative for current pod state, Governance for organizational policy, Git for repository history, KnowledgeOS for governed claim lifecycle; each authority type is strongest within its own dimension (e.g. OBSERVED can outrank DERIVED for runtime state).

anchor: Existing Document → Governance Object → Relationships → Document Projection. Draft→Review→Approve→Effective→Supersede.
statement: Work Package 4 (Formalize Governance): reverses the document/knowledge relationship so the document becomes a representation of governed knowledge rather than the sole record, with a target machine-addressable governance lifecycle.

anchor: check_nexus_version.sh → Rule: NEXUS_VERSION_COMPLIANCE; Checker = Implementation. Rule → Policy → Decision.
statement: Work Package 5 (Formalize Rules): gives existing deterministic checks stable rule identities separate from their script implementation, with a Rule schema (ID, version, description, scope, severity, applicability, expected state, checker reference, governance source) enabling Rule->Policy->Decision traceability.

anchor: Verification(V42) against Rule(R17:v3) which implements Policy(P8) established by Decision(D42) — a governance-grade assertion instead of 'Nexus check failed.'
statement: Work Package 6 (Connect Checks to Governance): transforms Check->PASS/FAIL into Decision->Policy->Rule->Checker->Verification, worked with the Nexus example, giving results organizational meaning.

anchor: EvidenceID with Source/CapturedAt/CapturedBy/Subject/Integrity/Provenance. Git commit ← Evidence Reference ← KnowledgeOS (evidence federation, not full duplication).
statement: Work Package 7 (Formalize Evidence): a common evidence-record schema and evidence federation (referencing rather than centralizing raw data).

anchor: Agent=Codex, Session=S182, Recommendation=R44, Action=A91, Commit=abc123, Evidence=E77.
statement: Work Package 8 (Connect Session Logging): evolves existing session/change logging into AgentSession->Action->Evidence with a worked full-identity-chain example, 'far stronger than a free-form session log.'

anchor: Decision -governs-> Policy -implementedBy-> Rule -verifiedBy-> Verification -supportedBy-> Evidence. Graph = Projection, not MasterDatabase.
statement: Work Package 9 (Introduce the Assurance Graph), 'the largest genuinely new architectural capability': makes relationships explicit via named node identities (DEC-42, POL-17, RULE-91, VER-182) and named edge semantics (governs, supports, evaluates, implementedBy, authorizedBy, producedBy — far better than generic 'relatedTo'), restating the graph must be treated as Projection, not MasterDatabase.

anchor: Task → Context Service {Governance, Knowledge, Evidence, Assurance, Graph, Authorization} → Context Package → Agent. Action → ContextID.
statement: Work Package 10 (Introduce Governed Context Service): the Context Service becomes the primary KnowledgeOS-Agent interface (Task->Relevant governed context), with every context package carrying a ContextID so an action can reference it and later reconstruction is possible.

anchor: KOS-ARCH-002: A governed material action must not bypass its applicable authorization policy.
statement: Work Package 11 (Formalize Action Authorization): examine existing authorization mechanisms, integrate where present, establish ActionRequest->Authorization->Execution where absent, formalized as KOS-ARCH-002, especially important for production/infrastructure/security/governance changes.

anchor: ValidFrom/ValidUntil as first-class concepts. A(t2) needs Context(t2), not Context(now).
statement: Work Package 12 (Introduce Temporal Semantics): distinguishes 'what is true now' from 'what was considered true when this action happened,' essential for audit.

anchor: KOS-ARCH-003: Every authoritative or assurance-relevant assertion must have discoverable provenance.
statement: Work Package 13 (Establish Provenance): the minimum traceability chain Source->Evidence->Claim->Decision (or for agents, Context->Recommendation->Authorization->Action->Evidence), formalized as KOS-ARCH-003; clarifies 'discoverable' does not require raw source stored inside KnowledgeOS — a reference may suffice.

anchor: EXPECTATION → RULE → CHECK → EVIDENCE → VERIFICATION → FINDING → DISPOSITION → EXPECTATION. The loop is more important than the graph.
statement: Work Package 14 (Build the Assurance Loop): the operational heart of KnowledgeOS, emphasizing 'closed-loop engineering assurance' is the real capability — the graph merely makes the loop navigable.

anchor: Finding → Disposition: Remediate, Accept Risk, Grant Exception, Change Policy, False Positive, Investigate.
statement: Work Package 15 (Establish Finding Disposition): a failed check must not simply disappear into a report but reach one of six governance-owned disposition outcomes.

anchor: AgentCapability ≠ Authorization. Deploy capability does not imply MayDeploy.
statement: Work Package 16 (Separate Human and Agent Authority): restates capability≠authorization must hold both technically and semantically.

anchor: KOS-ARCH-004: No agent implementation may receive a privileged semantic path unavailable to equivalent governed agents without an explicit policy reason.
statement: Work Package 17 (Normalize Claude and Codex): both should implement the same GET CONTEXT->REASON->RECOMMEND->REQUEST ACTION->AUTHORIZE->EXECUTE->REPORT EVIDENCE interaction model, formalized as KOS-ARCH-004, 'the formal version of the Claude/Codex symmetry principle.'

anchor: KnowledgeOS Domain → Port → Adapter → External System. GitPort, NexusPort, KubernetesPort.
statement: Work Package 18 (External-System Boundary): moves existing integrations conceptually behind ports so replacing e.g. Nexus only changes NexusAdapter->NewAdapter while the Assurance domain remains unchanged.

anchor: GraphProjectionHealthy, EvidenceIntegrityHealthy, OutboxHealthy, AuthorizationHealthy, ContextGenerationHealthy. KnowledgeOS → assures → KnowledgeOS.
statement: Work Package 19 (Platform Self-Assurance): KnowledgeOS should eventually verify its own architectural integrity via named deterministic self-health checks.

anchor: Rule 1: One authoritative owner per semantic concept. ... Rule 7: Derived projections must be rebuildable.
statement: Work Package 20 (Architecture Constitution): proposes capturing the discovered architectural rules as a formal KnowledgeOS Architecture Constitution (seven numbered rules consolidating one-authoritative-owner, no cross-context mutation, agent-local non-authority, governed authorization, deterministic-verification-preference, provenance-awareness, and projection-rebuildability), to become architectural fitness rules; diagrams the resulting recursion KnowledgeOS Architecture->Architecture Rules->Assurance Checkers->KnowledgeOS Verification->KnowledgeOS Architecture Health — 'the platform can therefore verify conformance to its own architecture.'

anchor: Phase 1 Authority+Identity → Phase 2 Knowledge+Governance → Phase 3 Evidence+Verification → Phase 4 Graph+Context → Phase 5 Authorization+Action → Phase 6 Continuous Self-Assurance.
statement: Defines a six-phase evolution sequence (not implementing all twenty work packages simultaneously), with each phase's rationale: Phase 1 establishes Identity/Ownership/Authority/Validity (without which the graph merely connects ambiguous objects); Phase 2 formalizes Decision/Policy/Exception/Claim with documents becoming projections; Phase 3 formalizes Evidence/Observation/Rule/Verification/Finding, connecting existing checks; Phase 4 introduces the Assurance Graph and Context Service once underlying semantics are stable (ordering important); Phase 5 connects Agent->Action->Authorization->Execution for governed agentic engineering; Phase 6 makes KnowledgeOS a subject of its own assurance model for continuous architecture governance.

anchor: CURRENT{Agents,Governance,Checks} → FORMALIZATION{Authority,Evidence,Rules} → RELATIONSHIP → ASSURANCE GRAPH → GOVERNED CONTEXT → GOVERNED AGENT → AUTHORIZED ACTION → EVIDENCE → VERIFICATION → GOVERNANCE.
statement: Summarizes the entire evolution as a single transformation-architecture diagram from current mechanisms through formalization, relationship-building, the graph, governed context/agent, authorized action, evidence, verification, and back to governance.

anchor: Do not: RewriteEverything, MakeEverythingAMicroservice, MakeTheGraphTheDatabaseOfEverything, PutAllKnowledgeIntoAgentMemory, LetLLMJudgmentReplaceDeterministicChecks, AllowAgentsToBypassAuthorization, CopyExternalSystemModelsIntoTheDomain.
statement: Lists seven tempting-but-incorrect implementation anti-patterns for the target system, derived from the entire delta analysis.

anchor: Before: EngineeringKnowledge = Files+Scripts+Memory+Logs+HumanUnderstanding. After: EngineeringKnowledge = GovernedSemanticObjects+Evidence+Relationships+ExplicitAuthority.
statement: States the deepest transformation as a Before/After redefinition of engineering knowledge itself, with files/scripts/agents remaining important interfaces and projections rather than the substance.

anchor: Documents → Machine-addressable semantic knowledge. AI Agent → Governed Engineering Actor. Compliance → Continuous Engineering Assurance.
statement: Explicitly rejects three reductive framings of the transformation — 'documents -> better documents' (it's documents -> machine-addressable semantic knowledge), 'chatbot -> better chatbot' (it's AI Agent -> Governed Engineering Actor), 'compliance engine' (it's compliance -> continuous engineering assurance spanning architecture/development/CI/deployment/runtime/evidence/governance) — and states the most concise description: KnowledgeOS evolves from a collection of AI-engineering knowledge/governance mechanisms into a governed semantic engineering platform.

anchor: Authority, Identity, Provenance, Relationships, Verification, Authorization — the most important changes are semantic, not technological.
statement: Step 143 verdict: the six most important semantic changes, after which existing Claude/Codex tooling, registry, deterministic checks, hooks, session logging, and engineering integrations can be progressively connected rather than replaced.

anchor: 1. Architecture workstreams ... 10. The first vertical slice. Governed Decision → Rule → Agent Context → Action → Evidence → Verification → Finding.
statement: Opens Step 144 (KnowledgeOS Evolution Roadmap): a ten-item roadmap-definition list (workstreams, dependencies, MVP boundary, what can start immediately, what awaits semantic decisions, artifact migration, untouched mechanisms, phase acceptance criteria, architecture fitness tests, first vertical slice); identifies the most important next decision as the first vertical slice — proving the architecture end-to-end with one real scenario (Governed Decision -> Rule -> Agent Context -> Action -> Evidence -> Verification -> Finding) as the reference implementation.

anchor: Do not build KnowledgeOS horizontally. Build one complete governed engineering loop.
statement: States the central roadmap rule and the full first-vertical-slice chain (Governed Decision->Applicable Rule->Governed Agent Context->Agent Recommendation->Action Request->Authorization->Execution->Evidence->Verification->Finding->Governance), 'the smallest slice that demonstrates the actual architectural thesis.'

anchor: Nexus as reference domain, not merely an example.
statement: Chooses Nexus as the vertical-slice subject because existing KnowledgeOS work already covers infrastructure discovery, version info, repository/blob-store info, runtime info, network info, migration requirements, governance questions, and architecture/change-management concerns — spanning Business/Architecture/Infrastructure/Security/Operations/Governance knowledge; but requires starting with Read->Analyze->Verify, not Agent->Production->Modify Nexus, to prove the semantic/assurance architecture without unnecessary operational risk.

anchor: Vertical Slice 0: Can KnowledgeOS determine the current governed state of Nexus and explain the evidence supporting that state?
statement: Vertical Slice 0 (read-only context query) with output schema (applicable governance, applicable knowledge, current observations, supporting evidence, applicable rules, verification results, open findings) and acceptance criterion that every context item carries Identity/Source/Authority/Validity/Provenance.

anchor: Vertical Slice 1: Evaluate a specific Nexus fitness rule (NexusVersionMustBeSupported). Rule → Nexus Adapter → Observation → Evidence → Verification → PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN.
statement: Vertical Slice 1, acceptance criterion: verification record must identify RuleID, RuleVersion, CheckerVersion, Subject, Evidence, Timestamp, Verdict — reproducible.

anchor: Vertical Slice 2: agent receives ContextPackage, produces Recommendation. Why did the agent make this recommendation? Recommendation → Context → Knowledge → Evidence → Governance.
statement: Vertical Slice 2 introduces the agent, with a worked recommendation example ('the planned Nexus upgrade should proceed only after infrastructure prerequisites X and Y have been verified') and the acceptance traversal explaining why the recommendation was made.

anchor: Vertical Slice 3: RequestAction evaluated by Authorization; agent does not directly execute. REQUESTED/AUTHORIZED/EXECUTED as three distinct states.
statement: Vertical Slice 3 introduces the action-request/authorization boundary with three distinguished states.

anchor: Vertical Slice 4: execute a safe non-production action (ReadNexusConfiguration / RunNexusVerification), producing ActionID/SessionID/AgentID/ContextID/AuthorizationID/EvidenceID.
statement: Vertical Slice 4, requiring the full identity chain to be produced by the action, then Action->Evidence.

anchor: Vertical Slice 5: Action → Evidence → Verification → PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, with failure raising FindingRaised.
statement: Vertical Slice 5, closing the loop by verifying resulting evidence and raising a Finding on failure; assembles the complete reference slice diagram (GOVERNANCE->Decision D42->Policy->Rule->CONTEXT SERVICE->AGENT->Recommendation->ActionRequest->AUTHORIZATION[ALLOW/DENY]->EXECUTION->EVIDENCE->VERIFICATION[PASS/FAIL]->{PASS, FAIL->FINDING->GOVERNANCE}) called 'the KnowledgeOS reference loop.'

anchor: WS1 Semantic Foundation ... WS7 Platform Self-Assurance.
statement: Organizes the roadmap into seven workstreams; WS1 (highest dependency priority) establishes stable IDs/object types/ownership/provenance/validity/lifecycle, with acceptance criteria being seven per-object questions (who owns it, what identifies it, lifecycle, what makes it authoritative, supporting evidence, validity window, what supersedes it) — if unanswerable, the object is not ready for implementation.

anchor: Do not migrate documents mechanically — ExtractSemanticObjects then LinkToOriginalArtifact.
statement: WS2 (Governance & Knowledge) migration principle: formalize Decision/Policy/Exception/Claim by extracting semantic objects from existing documents and linking back to the original artifact, preserving evidence/provenance rather than mechanical migration.

anchor: A deterministic check must answer 'which rule am I implementing?' — the transition from scripts to assurance components.
statement: WS3 (Evidence & Assurance) acceptance criterion connecting existing deterministic checks to formal Evidence/Observation/FitnessRule/Verification/Finding concepts.

anchor: Only after semantics are stable are GraphProjection and ContextService introduced — do not start with hundreds of relationship types.
statement: WS4 (Graph & Context): specifies a graph MVP with only seven relationship types (governs, appliesTo, supports, evaluates, implementedBy, producedBy, authorizedBy) and a minimal Context Service input (Task, Subject, Scope, Time, Agent) / output (Governance, Knowledge, Evidence, Rules, Findings, Permissions) schema.

anchor: The same KnowledgeOS task should be executable by Claude and Codex without changing the semantic governance model — only the adapter changes.
statement: WS5 (Agent Integration): the common agent contract Context->Reason->Recommendation->ActionRequest->Evidence, with Claude/Codex implementing their own adapters, tested by the cross-agent-portability acceptance criterion.

anchor: Read-only → Non-destructive mutation → Staging → Production with approval.
statement: WS6 (Authorization & Execution): a four-step incremental risk ladder for introducing the Request->Authorize->Execute governed action boundary, starting with low-risk read-only actions.

anchor: Architecture boundary check, Event/outbox consistency, Graph projection freshness, Evidence integrity, Agent contract compliance, Authorization bypass detection.
statement: WS7 (Self-Assurance): once the first loop works, KnowledgeOS becomes subject to its own assurance rules via six example self-checks.

anchor: WS1 → {WS2, WS3} → WS4 → WS5 → WS6 → WS7. Do not scale agent access before authority is defined. Governance → Assurance. Verdict → Evidence.
statement: Presents the workstream dependency graph and justifies the ordering: Agent Integration is not first because 'if the semantic foundation is unstable, the agents simply automate ambiguity' (do not scale agent access before authority is defined); the Graph is not first because a graph of poorly defined semantics produces 'fast confusion,' needing stable identities/ownership/relationships first; Governance is early because it defines ExpectedState (without which assurance has nothing authoritative to compare against, Governance->Assurance); Evidence is early because without it Verification becomes a bare assertion (Verdict->Evidence required).

anchor: MVP = one governed engineering scenario with complete traceability, not a full enterprise platform.
statement: Redefines the KnowledgeOS MVP and gives a ten-question success criterion (what was expected/why/what did the agent know/recommend/who authorized/what happened/what evidence proves it/was it compliant/what finding/what governance decision followed) — 'if all ten can be answered, the architecture has been proven.'

anchor: Golden Trace: Decision→Policy→Rule→Context→Agent→Recommendation→Authorization→Action→Evidence→Verification→Finding→Disposition. Trace(A)=Reconstruct(Decision,Context,Recommendation,Authorization,Action,Evidence,Verification).
statement: Introduces the 'Golden Trace' as the canonical demonstration artifact against which every implementation phase can be tested, with the reconstructability invariant that a successful golden trace must be reconstructable from stored state alone (no dependence on an LLM's conversational memory necessary); converts this into an architecture fitness rule 'every material governed agent action must have a reconstructable golden trace,' formalized as ArchitectureFitness=Check(GoldenTraceCompleteness).

anchor: AF-001: Every governed action has an AgentID. ... AF-007: Cross-context direct mutation is prohibited.
statement: Defines seven Architecture Fitness rules AF-001..007 (AgentID, AuthorizationID, ContextID, RuleVersion reference, evidence-or-recorded-unavailability, no agent-local authoritative source, no cross-context direct mutation), each intended to become an executable constraint (e.g. AF-003: Action.contextId IS NOT NULL) rather than a documentation rule, distinct from the earlier AFR-nn catalogue though overlapping in intent; diagrams the ultimate executable form: Architecture Constitution->Architecture Rules->Deterministic Checkers->Verification->Architecture Health, 'consistent with the deterministic-assurance direction already established in KnowledgeOS.'

anchor: Wave 1 high-value governance artifacts ... Wave 5 external-system observations. Structured Knowledge Object with sourceArtifact → Original Document (never delete).
statement: Defines a five-wave migration strategy avoiding a 'big bang' migration, with the rule that migration never means deleting old documents — a structured knowledge object retains a sourceArtifact reference preserving historical context.

anchor: Useful local context, Candidate knowledge, Verified knowledge, Obsolete, Unknown. Memory → CandidateClaim → Evidence → Verification → GovernedKnowledge. AgentOutput ⇏ Knowledge.
statement: Defines a five-way memory-item migration classification and the target promotion workflow, with the anti-automatic-promotion principle: the platform must never assume LLMGeneratedText=Truth — evidence and verification, not agent output alone, determine promotion.

anchor: P0 Semantic foundation ... P6 Self-assurance, each with an explicit Definition of Done.
statement: Condenses the roadmap into a seven-phase (P0-P6) table with objective and main result per phase, each with a one-sentence Definition of Done (P0: every core concept has owner/identity/lifecycle/authority/provenance/validity; P1: a governance decision can establish a machine-addressable expectation Decision->Policy->Rule; P2: a real deterministic check produces reproducible evidence-backed verification; P3: an agent can request context and receive only relevant governed information with provenance; P4: Claude and Codex consume the same semantic contract; P5: an agent cannot execute a controlled action without applicable authorization; P6: KnowledgeOS deterministically verifies aspects of its own architecture/operational integrity).

anchor: Make implicit knowledge explicit → addressable → verifiable → actionable → traceable back to authority.
statement: Summarizes the roadmap as a five-step evolutionary principle chain, then collapses the entire evolution into one final architecture loop diagram: GOVERNANCE -EXPECT-> KNOWLEDGE -INFORM-> AGENT -RECOMMEND-> AUTHORIZATION -ALLOW-> EXECUTION -OBSERVE-> EVIDENCE -VERIFY-> ASSURANCE -FEEDBACK-> GOVERNANCE.

anchor: Do not replace KnowledgeOS. Evolve it. One Golden Trace. Nexus.
statement: Step 144 verdict: the concrete evolution strategy is not a platform-wide rewrite but one Golden Trace for one real engineering scenario, with Nexus as the best currently identified reference scenario because it crosses infrastructure, architecture, governance, evidence, assurance, and agent-assisted engineering.

anchor: The exact scenario, actors, bounded contexts, input state, commands, domain events, evidence, graph relationships, authorization points, verification rules, expected outputs, failure paths, audit reconstruction, architecture fitness criteria.
statement: Opens Step 145 (The Golden Trace Specification): defines the Golden Trace as an actual architectural specification (not just a diagram) covering fourteen elements, to produce the first executable KnowledgeOS reference architecture against which Claude, Codex, and the existing EKS mechanisms can be tested.

anchor: GT-NEXUS-001: Human, Agent, KnowledgeOS, Governance, Engineering system, Assurance.
statement: Names the reference scenario GT-NEXUS-001 ('an agent must determine whether a planned engineering change to Nexus can proceed under the applicable governance and technical constraints,' analysis/read-only-verification only, no production mutation) and its six logical actors (Human, Agent, KnowledgeOS, Governance, Engineering system, Assurance) with their responsibilities.

anchor: Decision D-001, Policy P-001, Rule R-001, Subject NEXUS-001 — all with stable identity.
statement: Establishes the Golden Trace initial state: Decision (status=EFFECTIVE, scope=Nexus, validFrom=T1, authority=Architecture Governance), Knowledge about Nexus (identity, environment, version, repository configuration, infrastructure references, known constraints, each claim with provenance), and Rule R-001 (appliesTo, expected condition, severity, checker, version) as 'an addressable assurance object,' not merely a paragraph of text.

anchor: TaskRequest → GetGovernedContext → ContextPackage CTX-001.
statement: Walks through the agent request (TaskRequest with task/subject/scope/actor/requested operation=ASSESS) and context construction (agent requests GetGovernedContext rather than assembling context itself; Context Service retrieves applicable decisions, relevant claims, applicable rules/findings, current evidence, and agent permissions, producing ContextPackage CTX-001 with ContextVersion=V1).

anchor: Recommendation REC-001: 'the change appears permissible, subject to verification...' — a recommendation, not a governance decision.
statement: Records the agent's first recommendation with schema (agent, session, context, reasoning reference, proposed action, timestamp), explicitly noting the exact storage of chain-of-thought is not prescribed — only decision/provenance metadata is required, not necessarily private internal reasoning.

anchor: Verify(R-001): Assurance → Checker → Nexus Adapter → Nexus → Observation (version=X, observedAt=T2). Observation is not automatically knowledge.
statement: Walks through verification request/checker execution/observation, creating Evidence E-001 (source, subject, observedAt, capturedBy, externalReference, integrity metadata), then Verification V-001 comparing Expected(R-001) against Observed(E-001) with schema (rule, ruleVersion, checkerVersion, subject, evidence, executionTime, verdict) and three possible verdicts PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN.

anchor: Rule=R-001, Evidence=insufficient, Verdict=UNKNOWN, Reason=source unavailable — different from both PASS and FAIL.
statement: Worked UNKNOWN-verdict example (Nexus unreachable), reinforcing UNKNOWN as a distinct, explicitly supported state; agent's second recommendation after receiving the verification result ('current evidence supports proceeding with the planned assessment, but production execution remains subject to required approval'), restating Recommendation ≠ Authorization.

anchor: ActionRequest A-001 = ReadNexusConfiguration (deliberately low-risk). Authorization AUTH-001 evaluated from Agent+Human delegation+Action+Subject+Environment+Policy.
statement: Specifies the first Golden Trace action request as a deliberately low-risk read-only operation and the authorization schema (decision=ALLOW, actor, action, scope, authority, validity, conditions) — more than a boolean.

anchor: Authorized Action → Nexus Adapter → Nexus. ExecutionID EX-001 → EvidenceID E-002. E-002 → Rule → Verification V-002 — actions themselves can produce assurance evidence.
statement: Walks through action execution and second-round verification, then the finding/disposition path if V-002=FAIL: Finding F-001 (verification, rule, subject, severity, evidence, status=OPEN) routed to Governance Review yielding disposition REMEDIATE/EXCEPTION/RISK ACCEPTED.

anchor: D-001→P-001→R-001→CTX-001→REC-001→A-001→AUTH-001→EX-001→E-002→V-002→{PASS→Completed, FAIL→F-001→Governance→Disposition}
statement: Presents the complete Golden Trace as one semantic chain — 'the first complete semantic trace' — and its graph representation with fourteen named edges (governs, establishes, appliesTo, verifiedBy, supportedBy, contains, basedOn, requestedBy, authorizedBy, executedAs, produced, evaluatedBy, raises), concluding 'now the graph has genuine semantic value.'

anchor: DecisionID, PolicyID, RuleID, SubjectID, ContextID, AgentID, SessionID, RecommendationID, ActionID, AuthorizationID, ExecutionID, EvidenceID, VerificationID, FindingID. TraceID (GT-NEXUS-001) ≠ ActionID ≠ EvidenceID.
statement: Defines the fourteen-item minimum identity set the model must support (not every workflow requires every one) and introduces TraceID as a correlation identifier distinct from any entity ID — the trace represents the workflow, entities represent operations inside it.

anchor: ContextRequested, ContextProvided, RecommendationCreated, ..., DispositionRecorded — an operational history that does not require full event sourcing.
statement: Represents the trace as a thirteen-event sequence, explicitly not requiring full event sourcing — only that important lifecycle transitions be reconstructable, via state+audit records, domain events, outbox, or event sourcing depending on actual requirements.

anchor: createdAt, effectiveAt, observedAt, executedAt — not collapsed into one generic timestamp. Knowledge(T2) valid when Action(T4) occurred?
statement: Requires a four-timestamp temporal model per record and a worked example (Policy effective T1, context T2, observation T3, action T4, verification T5) enabling the question of whether knowledge from T2 was still valid at action time T4; formalizes a temporal-validity precondition (Policy.validAt(T4)?, Authorization.validAt(T4)?, Context.validAt(T4)?) as a deterministic precondition before execution.

anchor: F1 Context unavailable, F2 Rule fails, F3 Evidence unavailable, F4 Authorization denied, F5 Execution failure.
statement: Defines five named failure paths the reference implementation must demonstrate (not only success): F1 ContextRequest->UNAVAILABLE (with the hard invariant NoContext=>NoExecution for high-risk actions); F2 Verification->FAIL (agent may recommend remediation, but FAIL≠AgentDecision, cannot be overridden); F3 Verification->UNKNOWN (must not be reinterpreted as PASS — platform invariant UNKNOWN≠PASS); F4 ActionRequest->DENY (execution must not occur through the governed path, mechanically enforceable); F5 Authorized->ExecutionFailed (authorization does not imply successful execution, leading to Evidence->Finding/Incident).

anchor: GT-001 Action.contextID≠null. GT-002 Action.authorizationID≠null. GT-003..008 covering rule version, evidence-or-UNKNOWN, denied/expired-authorization-cannot-execute, recommendation≠authorization, agent memory not authoritative through use.
statement: Defines eight trace-level invariants GT-001..GT-008 concretizing the reference architecture: every material action references a context and has authorization; every verification identifies its exact rule version and has evidence or an explicit UNKNOWN reason; a denied or expired authorization cannot execute; agent recommendation ≠ governance authorization; agent memory cannot become authoritative merely through use.

anchor: GG-001..005: every verification points to a rule and its evidence; every rule has applicability; every governed action traces to authorization; every finding traces to verification.
statement: Defines five graph invariants GG-001..GG-005 for the Assurance Graph representation of the trace.

anchor: GE-001..005: evidence has source, subject, capture time, provenance; evidence cannot silently change after verification.
statement: Defines five evidence invariants GE-001..GE-005.

anchor: GC-001..005: context is scoped, has identity, has temporal semantics where required, identifies its sources, does not itself become a competing source of truth.
statement: Defines five context invariants GC-001..GC-005.

anchor: GA-001..005: agent identity/session explicit; recommendation distinguishable from action; action distinguishable from authorization; Claude and Codex consume the same semantic contract.
statement: Defines five agent invariants GA-001..GA-005.

anchor: GIVEN effective governance decision... WHEN agent requests governed context... THEN context returned with identity and provenance... [through verification/authorization/action/finding].
statement: Converts the entire scenario into a Given/When/Then integration-test acceptance specification, 'now a testable architecture.'

anchor: Golden Trace = ReferenceImplementation. How does this capability fit into the Golden Trace model?
statement: States once implemented, the Golden Trace becomes the reference implementation, and any future capability that cannot answer 'how does this fit into the Golden Trace model' should have its place in the core architecture questioned.

anchor: Task, Context, Recommendation, Action, Authorization, Execution, Observation, Evidence, Verification, Finding, Disposition, Trace.
statement: Lists twelve concepts the Golden Trace exercise exposed as needing explicit treatment, added to the semantic model; presents an updated, considerably more complete KnowledgeOS semantic model organized under Governance{Decision,Policy,Exception,Disposition}, Knowledge{Claim,KnowledgeState,Context}, Assurance{Rule,Verification,Finding}, Evidence{Observation,Evidence,Provenance}, Agent{Agent,Session,Task,Recommendation,Action,Authorization,Execution}, Cross-context{Assurance Graph}.

anchor: Observation ≠ Evidence ≠ Verification ≠ Finding, forming Observation→Evidence→Verification→Finding. Task ≠ Recommendation ≠ Action ≠ Authorization ≠ Execution, forming Task→Recommendation→Action→Authorization→Execution.
statement: States two strict five-stage lifecycle distinctions that must remain strict — the observation-to-finding chain and the task-to-execution chain — 'essential for governed agents.'

anchor: Expectation → Context → Reasoning → Authorization → Execution → Evidence → Verification → Disposition.
statement: States the architecture has moved beyond 'Knowledge+AI+Governance' to become a state-transition system, boxing this eight-stage central behavioral model of KnowledgeOS.

anchor: Every material engineering action can be reconstructed from authority+context+agent+authorization+execution+evidence+verification.
statement: Step 145 verdict: the Golden Trace's key property is full reconstructability, offered as the architectural definition of a 'governed engineering action.'

anchor: Aggregates, Entities, Value Objects, Domain Events and Invariants. What each Aggregate is allowed to change.
statement: Opens Step 146 (Golden Trace -> Domain Model): formalizes the Golden Trace's exposed objects into tactical DDD constructs, with the critical decisions being which objects are Aggregates, transaction boundaries, which IDs are Value Objects, which relationships belong inside an Aggregate vs only in the Graph, which events cross bounded-context boundaries, and what each Aggregate may change — to implement the first Golden Trace without collapsing bounded contexts into one object model.

anchor: Aggregate = ConsistencyBoundary. Entity ≠ Aggregate.
statement: States the first principle for this step and lists the candidate aggregate map (Governance{Decision,Policy,Exception,Disposition}, Knowledge{Claim,KnowledgeState}, Assurance{Rule,Verification,Finding}, Evidence{Evidence,Observation}, Agent{Agent,Session,Task,Recommendation,Action,Authorization,Execution}), explicitly warning against assuming each line is automatically one Aggregate.

anchor: D-INV-001..004: stable identity; only authorized authority makes it effective; effective Decision cannot be silently modified; supersession preserves historical traceability.
statement: Defines the DecisionAggregate with candidate lifecycle DRAFT->UNDER_REVIEW->APPROVED->EFFECTIVE->SUPERSEDED (potential terminal RETIRED) and four numbered invariants D-INV-001..004.

anchor: Decision answers 'what was decided'; Policy answers 'what rule or expectation governs behavior.' Decision → establishes → Policy (reference, not containment).
statement: Separates Policy from Decision as its own aggregate, connected by reference rather than containment; defines Exception's own lifecycle (REQUESTED->REVIEWED->APPROVED->ACTIVE->EXPIRED, potentially REJECTED) with the critical invariant Exception ≠ DeleteRule — Rule+Exception->ModifiedApplicability, the original rule remaining historically visible.

anchor: Claim schema (ClaimID, subject, predicate, value, status, validity, provenance, evidence references). VERIFIED claim ≠ GOVERNANCE AUTHORITY.
statement: Defines the KnowledgeClaimAggregate schema and lifecycle (PROPOSED->SUPPORTED->VERIFIED->EFFECTIVE, potential DISPUTED/SUPERSEDED/REJECTED), with the important separation that a verified observational claim (e.g. 'Nexus currently reports version 3.69') does not establish a governance requirement ('Nexus must run version 3.70') — the latter comes only from Governance.

anchor: RuleAggregate owns RuleID/Version/Applicability/ExpectedCondition/Severity/CheckerReference/Lifecycle. R42:v1 and R42:v2 are distinct semantic versions.
statement: Defines the RuleAggregate as immutable by version, with a verification referencing exactly one version.

anchor: Verification = (VerificationID, RuleID+Version, Subject, CheckerVersion, EvidenceReferences, ExecutedAt, Verdict, ExecutionContext). Immutable once completed — Verification_new, not overwrite.
statement: Defines the VerificationAggregate schema answering what/against-which-rule/using-which-checker/using-which-evidence/with-what-result, immutable after completion for auditability.

anchor: Finding schema (FindingID, sourceVerification, severity, status, owner, disposition, lifecycle). OPEN→ACKNOWLEDGED→IN_REMEDIATION→RESOLVED, or ACCEPTED.
statement: Defines the FindingAggregate as a structured object (not a text field on Verification) with its own lifecycle.

anchor: Evidence already used for verification must not be silently altered — E_new, not E_old ← newState. Observation is what an external system reports; Evidence is the retained provenance-bearing representation.
statement: Defines the EvidenceAggregate schema and its key immutability invariant, and reiterates Observation ≠ Evidence — one observation may become one evidence item but the semantic distinction remains (Nexus->Observation->Evidence).

anchor: AgentAggregate for identity/configuration; SessionAggregate for one interaction lifecycle; ActionAggregate for a proposed/executed action — Session should reference, not transactionally contain, its Actions.
statement: Decomposes the Agent context into three separate aggregates; defines Agent schema (AgentID, AgentType, Provider, Capabilities, Status, implementation-specific config staying outside the domain) and Session schema (SessionID, AgentID, HumanPrincipal, startedAt, endedAt, ContextReferences, Actions), warning a long-running session with dozens/hundreds of actions should reference rather than transactionally contain them all — 'an important Aggregate boundary decision.'

anchor: Task schema (TaskID, objective, subject, scope, requester, status). Recommendation ≠ Action — the agent can recommend without requesting execution.
statement: Defines Task and Recommendation schemas (Recommendation: RecommendationID, TaskID, ContextID, proposedOutcome, supportingReferences, agent, timestamp), noting detailed private reasoning need not be persisted as part of the domain model.

anchor: A-INV-001..005: stable identity; references originating context; cannot execute without required authorization; execution result cannot be represented as authorization; execution produces traceable evidence where applicable.
statement: Defines the ActionAggregate lifecycle (REQUESTED->AUTHORIZED->EXECUTING->EXECUTED, failure paths DENIED/FAILED/CANCELLED) and five action invariants A-INV-001..005.

anchor: Authorization schema (AuthorizationID, ActionID, Principal, authority, scope, conditions, validFrom, validUntil, decision). Once consumed, historically stable — NewAuthorization or AuthorizationRevoked, not mutation.
statement: Defines the AuthorizationAggregate as its own consistency boundary answering 'is this specific action allowed under the applicable authority and conditions.'

anchor: Action = intent. Execution = fact. Action may have been valid even if Execution failed.
statement: Distinguishes Action (intent) from Execution (fact) with a worked example (Action A42 operation=ReadNexusConfiguration; Execution E42 status=SUCCESS, startedAt/completedAt, externalReference).

anchor: Reference other Aggregates by identity (Action.authorizationId=AUTH-42, not embedding the Authorization object). Reference other Bounded Contexts through stable contracts/IDs, not shared domain object graphs (Verification → RuleID, not Governance.RuleEntity).
statement: States the DDD rule for cross-aggregate and cross-context references — by identity/contract, never by embedding the full object.

anchor: DecisionID, PolicyID, RuleID, ClaimID, EvidenceID, VerificationID, FindingID, AgentID, SessionID, TaskID, ActionID, AuthorizationID, ExecutionID, ContextID, TraceID — as typed Value Objects, not raw strings.
statement: Lists fifteen candidate typed-ID value objects, arguing strong typing prevents accidental cross-type assignment (e.g. EvidenceID=RuleID) at compile time and makes APIs self-documenting; adds ValidityPeriod (validFrom, validUntil, enforcing validFrom<validUntil), Scope (organization, system, environment, resource — dimensions domain-specific), and Provenance (source, capturedBy, capturedAt, reference) as further value-object candidates, the latter conceptually shared across contexts but not necessarily one shared implementation class.

anchor: Resist a large SharedKernel — a tiny one might hold only primitive identity conventions/timestamps/correlation identifiers. Prefer Published Language (e.g. DecisionReference) over importing Governance's internal entity.
statement: Warns Governance and Assurance should not share rich domain classes merely because of similar words; recommends a Published Language contract (e.g. DecisionReference: id, status, validity, authority) for cross-context consumption instead of importing internal entities.

anchor: DecisionBecameEffective, ClaimVerified, EvidenceCaptured, VerificationCompleted, FindingRaised, ActionRequested, ActionExecuted, ActionAuthorized — each owned by the context that owns the transition.
statement: Lists eight domain events the Golden Trace naturally produces, restating event ownership (Governance->DecisionBecameEffective, not KnowledgeOS->DecisionBecameEffective — 'the platform transports the event, the domain owns its meaning'); assembles the full reference Golden Trace event stream (thirteen events from DecisionBecameEffective through FindingRaised), noting not every event necessarily needs external publication.

anchor: DomainEvent describes a state transition; IntegrationEvent is a message deliberately published to another context/system. Internal DecisionBecameEffective vs external EffectiveDecisionPublished, independently versioned.
statement: Distinguishes domain events from integration events with a worked example showing they can share a conceptual source but must not be assumed identical or identically versioned.

anchor: GOVERNANCE{DecisionAggregate,PolicyAggregate,ExceptionAggregate}; KNOWLEDGE{ClaimAggregate}; EVIDENCE{EvidenceAggregate}; ASSURANCE{RuleAggregate,VerificationAggregate,FindingAggregate}; AGENT{AgentAggregate,SessionAggregate,TaskAggregate,RecommendationAggregate,ActionAggregate,AuthorizationAggregate}; EXECUTION{ExecutionRecord}.
statement: Presents a consolidated aggregate ownership map, explicitly still a candidate model, not yet final.

anchor: Is Execution part of Agent/Action, or an Engineering Execution context? Action → requests → Engineering System → produces → Execution Fact → Evidence.
statement: Raises the unresolved question of Execution's context ownership, argues for treating it as belonging to the engineering environment (Kubernetes/Nexus authoritative for what happened operationally, KnowledgeOS recording only the reference and evidence), and gives the recommended interim interpretation: Action belongs to Agent/Action management, ExecutionFact is produced by the Engineering integration.

anchor: DM-001: An Aggregate exists to protect a consistency boundary, not to model every semantic relationship. What invariant would be broken if these objects were updated separately?
statement: Formalizes the practical aggregate-boundary test as invariant DM-001, applied to four worked pairs: Action+Authorization (separate — different lifecycle/authority/expiration/audit requirements, Action->AuthorizationID); Rule+Verification (separate — Rule persists over time, Verification is one execution against one version); Evidence+Verification (separate — one evidence item can support multiple verifications, captured only in the graph); Decision+Policy (separate — one Decision may establish multiple policies, one Policy may outlive its originating decision document, Decision->PolicyReference).

anchor: Aggregate answers 'what must change consistently?' Graph answers 'what is related to what?' Aggregate ≠ Graph.
statement: States this as perhaps the most important DDD distinction of the step, with a worked example — the graph can hold Decision D42 -governs-> Policy P8, -appliesTo-> Nexus, -motivatedBy-> Finding F2 as cross-context relationships without the Decision Aggregate needing to contain Policy+Nexus+Finding.

anchor: Transaction □ one Aggregate, not Transaction □ {Governance, Knowledge, Evidence, Assurance, Agent} — the latter destroys bounded-context autonomy.
statement: Recommends transactions scoped to one aggregate, with cross-context propagation via events (Governance transaction commits Decision, then DecisionBecameEffective propagates, Knowledge and Assurance react independently) yielding eventual consistency without a distributed transaction; connects graph updates to the same event/outbox mechanism (Outbox->Replay if projection fails), consistent with the runtime architecture from Step 141.

anchor: GOVERNANCE{Decision,Policy}→KNOWLEDGE{Claim}→ASSURANCE{Rule,Verification→Finding}; AGENT{Task,Recommendation,Action→Authorization→Execution→Evidence→Verification}.
statement: Presents the domain model summary diagram produced by the Golden Trace exercise, a much more precise model than the earlier conceptual sketches.

anchor: DM-002: agent recommendation is never itself an authorization. DM-003: authorization is never evidence an action succeeded. DM-004: an execution fact is never equivalent to a governance decision. DM-005: verification must identify the exact rule version. DM-006: evidence used by assurance must remain historically reconstructable. DM-007: cross-context relationships do not imply aggregate ownership.
statement: Lists six core domain invariants DM-002..DM-007 emerging from the model.

anchor: Intent → Recommendation → Authorization → Execution → Observation → Evidence → Verification → Finding → Disposition. Decision → Policy → Rule → ExpectedState. The two chains meet at Verification.
statement: States the complete semantic chain distinguishes an engineering-intent chain from a governance-expectation chain, meeting at Verification; reframes the entire platform as the intersection of a Governance flow (Decision->Policy->Rule->Expectation), an Engineering flow (Intent->Action->Execution->Observation->Evidence), and an Assurance bridge (Expectation+Evidence->Verification->Finding) — 'a much stronger definition of KnowledgeOS than simply AI engineering knowledge management.'

anchor: Aggregates protect local invariants; Events/contracts connect contexts; the Assurance Graph represents cross-context relationships.
statement: Step 146 verdict: the central design decision answering 'where should KnowledgeOS put the boundaries?'

anchor: Commands + DomainEvents + IntegrationEvents + Queries + Contracts. Which communication must be synchronous, which asynchronous, which must never cross a boundary at all?
statement: Opens Step 147 (Domain Events & Integration Contracts): defines exactly how the aggregates communicate, posing the synchronous/asynchronous/never-cross question before designing APIs and persistence.

anchor: Aggregates communicate through explicit contracts, not shared object graphs. Command/Query/Domain Event/Integration Event.
statement: States the guiding principle and defines four interaction mechanisms with meaning/direction (Command=please perform, request; Query=tell me current information, read; Domain Event=something meaningful happened, internal fact; Integration Event=another context needs to know, cross-boundary fact); states Query -> no domain mutation; distinguishes Command=Intent from Event=Fact.

anchor: Governance -> Domain Event -> Integration Event -> Knowledge. Without the distinction, the event bus becomes a dumping ground of SomethingHappenedEvent.
statement: Argues domain events and integration events must be distinguished (e.g. DecisionBecameEffective internally vs EffectiveDecisionPublished across the boundary) to avoid consumers coupling to internal implementation details; exposes only meaningful cross-context contracts.

anchor: Governance: CreateDecision..ExpireException / DecisionCreated..ExceptionExpired. Knowledge: CreateClaim../ClaimCreated... Evidence: CaptureObservation../ObservationCaptured... Assurance: RegisterRule../RuleActivated... Agent: StartSession../SessionStarted... Authorization: EvaluateAuthorization../ActionAuthorized... Action: PrepareAction/AuthorizeAction/ExecuteAuthorizedAction/CancelAction. Execution: ExecutionStarted/Completed/Failed/Cancelled.
statement: Lists candidate command/event pairs for each bounded context; specifically separates the Action boundary's RequestAction from actual execution via PrepareAction/AuthorizeAction/ExecuteAuthorizedAction/CancelAction, preventing RequestAction from silently becoming ExecuteAction; notes Execution events likely originate from an external engineering-system adapter.

anchor: DecisionBecameEffective → PolicyActivated → RuleActivated → ContextRequested → ContextProvided → VerificationRequested → EvidenceCaptured → VerificationCompleted → RecommendationCreated → ActionRequested → AuthorizationEvaluated → {DENIED, AUTHORIZED → ActionExecutionRequested → Execution → EvidenceCaptured → VerificationCompleted → {PASS, FAIL → FindingRaised}}.
statement: Assembles the full reference Golden Trace event chain with an explicit authorization branch.

anchor: Synchronous: GetContext, EvaluateAuthorization, GetVerificationStatus. Asynchronous: EvidenceIngestion, GraphProjection, Notification, LongRunningVerification.
statement: Gives a rule for choosing synchronous (caller needs immediate response) vs asynchronous (independent processing) interactions; states authorization should normally be synchronous (no fire-and-forget authorization for high-risk actions), execution can be asynchronous (deployments/migrations/long-running verification), context retrieval should normally be synchronous (agent needs an answer before reasoning), and graph updates can be asynchronous via Domain State->Outbox->Projection->Graph for eventual consistency.

anchor: | Operation | Consistency | Decision activation: Strong/local. Graph projection, search index, notifications, analytics: Eventual.
statement: Presents a nine-row consistency classification table across operations, arguing this is much healthier than making everything strongly consistent; requires a command to normally modify one Aggregate within one transaction, with the event leaving the transaction boundary afterward.

anchor: Transaction{Decision state change + Outbox event} commits together, preventing the classic dual-write problem (DB updated -> publish event -> BROKER FAILURE -> Knowledge/Graph never learns).
statement: Reiterates the transactional-outbox pattern with a worked dual-write-failure illustration; requires event consumers to be idempotent (Consumer(EventID) processing a duplicate delivery produces no duplicate semantic effect).

anchor: EventEnvelope: eventId, eventType, eventVersion, occurredAt, producer, correlationId, causationId, payload. CorrelationID = which workflow; CausationID = which event/action caused this one.
statement: Defines the full event envelope schema and distinguishes CorrelationID (workflow membership, e.g. Trace GT-NEXUS-001) from CausationID (direct cause), each Golden Trace event retaining causation relationships; requires event versioning (EventType+EventVersion, e.g. VerificationCompleted:v1 -> v2) with AdditiveChange preferred before BreakingChange, and NewVersion when a breaking semantic change is unavoidable.

anchor: EffectiveDecision{decisionId,authority,scope,effectiveAt,policyReferences} — internal persistence fields, workflow objects, UI data, and implementation details deliberately absent.
statement: Gives six worked minimal integration-contract payload schemas: EffectiveDecision, EvidenceRegistered (evidenceId, subject, source, capturedAt, reference, provenance), VerificationCompleted (verificationId, ruleId, ruleVersion, subject, verdict, evidenceReferences, completedAt), FindingRaised (findingId, verificationId, ruleId, subject, severity, raisedAt — Governance can use without importing Assurance internals), ActionRequested (actionId, subject, operation, requestedBy, contextId, traceId, requestedAt), ActionAuthorized (authorizationId, actionId, authority, scope, conditions, validUntil — execution layer needs only this, not the full Authorization aggregate).

anchor: IC-001: External API models must not cross into the domain layer unchanged.
statement: Interaction-contract invariant IC-001, illustrated by the Nexus adapter translating a Nexus API response into NexusObservation and ultimately EvidenceRegistered — the external API contract terminates at the adapter.

anchor: GetNexusGovernedContext composing Governance/Knowledge/Evidence/Assurance read models + Graph → ContextPackage — a natural CQRS separation, but do not overengineer (CQRS+EventSourcing+Microservices are not required merely because events exist).
statement: Describes query-side composition as a natural place for CQRS-style separation while warning against overengineering — the architecture needs separation of concerns, not fashionable infrastructure, achievable within a modular application; proposes a specialized ContextIndex read model (subject, applicable decisions, applicable rules, current claims, recent evidence, open findings) to improve agent latency, with a ContextCache explicitly Cache≠Authority, carrying Validity/SourceVersion, and stale-context protection requiring ContextAge<threshold or matching ContextVersion before high-risk actions.

anchor: CanExecute(Action) = AuthorizationValid ∧ ContextValid ∧ RequiredAssurancePassed ∧ SubjectAvailable.
statement: Defines a deterministic execution-gate precondition combining Authorization, Context, Assurance, and Subject checks, diagrammed as Action -> {Authorization, Context, Assurance} -> EXECUTE, 'where the previously separate architecture concepts converge.'

anchor: AUTHORIZATION_DENIED, CONTEXT_EXPIRED, ASSURANCE_FAILED, REQUIRED_EVIDENCE_MISSING, SUBJECT_UNAVAILABLE — not a bare ERROR. 'Execution was denied because authorization expired' vs 'API returned 403.'
statement: Requires specific, agent-legible failure reasons when CanExecute=false rather than a generic error, giving the agent a domain-level explanation instead of a raw status code.

anchor: Graph consumer listens to DecisionApproved/PolicyActivated/EvidenceRegistered/VerificationCompleted/FindingRaised/ActionAuthorized/ActionExecuted and creates GraphNodes/GraphEdges. If projection fails, authoritative state remains safe and the graph is only temporarily stale.
statement: Worked graph-projection example (VerificationCompleted(V42) creating V42-evaluates->R17, -appliesTo->Nexus, -supportedBy->E81) and the graph-staleness-safety argument — the core domain remains correct even if the graph is temporarily stale, 'exactly why the graph should not be the transactional source of truth.'

anchor: IC-002: Cross-context projections may be eventually consistent unless a specific business invariant requires synchronous consistency.
statement: Interaction-contract invariant IC-002.

anchor: Command → AuthorizationPolicy. ApproveDecision requires Governance authority; RequestAction may require an authenticated agent; ExecuteProductionAction requires stronger authority.
statement: States commands themselves must be authorized, with different commands requiring different authority levels.

anchor: Agent Capabilities: QueryContext, RequestVerification, CreateRecommendation, RequestAction, ReadEvidence — ExecuteProductionAction not generally available. AgentCapability ⊆ PlatformCapability. AuthorizedCapability = Capability ∩ Policy ∩ Scope.
statement: Defines the agent command boundary as a restricted capability set rather than arbitrary domain-command invocation, formalizing AgentCapability ⊆ PlatformCapability and the actual permission as the intersection of capability, policy, and scope.

anchor: AGENT -Agent API-> APPLICATION -Domain Commands-> DOMAIN -Domain Events-> INTEGRATION LAYER -Integration Events-> {Knowledge, Assurance, Governance} -> Projections.
statement: Presents the four-layer contract hierarchy and three fundamental flows: Command flow (Intent->Command->Aggregate), Event flow (Aggregate->Event->OtherContexts), Query flow (Agent->Query->ReadModels) — 'this separation is fundamental.'

anchor: Human → Agent → QueryContext → Context Service {query Governance/Knowledge/Assurance/Evidence} → ContextPackage → reasoning → Recommendation → RequestAction → Authorization {DENY→stop, ALLOW→ExecuteAction} → External System → Evidence → Verification {PASS, FAIL→Finding→Governance}.
statement: Assembles the complete Golden-Trace interaction-model diagram combining commands, queries, and events into one end-to-end flow.

anchor: IC-003: Commands express intent; events express facts. IC-004: Queries do not mutate domain state. IC-005: Cross-context communication uses published contracts. IC-006: External API models terminate at adapters. IC-007: Consumers of events must be idempotent. IC-008: High-risk authorization must be evaluated before execution. IC-009: The graph may be stale temporarily but must be rebuildable. IC-010: A recommendation cannot directly trigger an execution without the required action/authorization path.
statement: Defines eight interaction invariants IC-003..IC-010 consolidating the step's principles.

anchor: Commands → Aggregates → Events → Context Projections. Queries → Governed Read Models → Agent. Action → Authorization → Execution → Evidence → Verification.
statement: Step 147 verdict: boxes the essential interaction architecture in three parts (write/command flow, query flow, execution flow), giving a complete interaction model without premature commitment to a specific broker, database, or microservice architecture.

anchor: What is the minimum stable KnowledgeOS contract that all agents can rely upon, independent of internal implementation?
statement: Opens Step 148 (API & Contract Architecture): defines external interfaces for Claude, Codex, CI/CD, engineering systems, governance clients, assurance checkers, and graph consumers, aiming to produce the KnowledgeOS Platform API Contract v1 and establish the boundary between existing .claude/.codex mechanisms and the future centralized platform.

anchor: API ≠ Domain Model. API ≠ Database Schema. The API should expose capabilities and governed interactions, not internal implementation structures.
statement: States the core API architecture principle and organizes the API around capability domains (Knowledge, Governance, Context, Assurance, Evidence, Agent, Action, Authorization) rather than raw database-table-style resources (/decisions, /policies, /evidence, /actions).

anchor: GetGovernedContext: ContextRequest{traceId,agentId,taskId,subject,scope,requestedAt,purpose} → ContextPackage{contextId,generatedAt,validUntil,governance,knowledge,rules,evidence,findings,permissions,provenance}. Minimum sufficient governed context, not maximum available context.
statement: Designates the Context API as the most important initial API (principal AI-agent interface), gives detailed request/response schemas including a 'purpose' field (same subject may need different context per task), requires every context item to be traceable to source/inclusion-reason/authority/validity (ContextItem->SourceReference), and states the context-minimization principle for reasoning/performance/security/explainability; explicitly declines to freeze REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC — 'a governed Context capability must exist' is the stable decision, protocol is implementation detail.

anchor: Agent API: getContext, getKnowledge, getEvidence, requestVerification, createRecommendation, requestAction, getActionStatus.
statement: Sketches the shared Claude/Codex Agent API capability set, noting the capability boundary matters more than endpoint count; defines agent registration (RegisterAgent with agentId, agentType, provider, capabilities, version, environment) and distinguishes AgentType from AgentInstance for audit purposes; defines capability declaration (e.g. QUERY_CONTEXT) as merely asserting technical capability, not permission — MayPerform = DeclaredCapability ∧ Policy ∧ Principal ∧ Scope ∧ Context, restating Capability ≠ Permission.

anchor: RequestVerification → VerificationReference; synchronous VerificationResult vs asynchronous VerificationJob+GetVerification.
statement: Defines the Verification API request/response for both synchronous and long-running checks.

anchor: RegisterEvidence(source,subject,observedAt,reference,provenance) → EvidenceID. Avoid PUT /evidence/123 as generic update — prefer RegisterEvidence and SupersedeEvidence.
statement: Defines the Evidence API and warns against treating evidence as freely mutable given its historical significance.

anchor: Governance API: CreateDecision, SubmitDecision, ApproveDecision, ActivateDecision, SupersedeDecision — never PATCH decision.status=EFFECTIVE. State transitions should be expressed as domain operations, not arbitrary field updates.
statement: Defines the Governance API and states the important API principle contrasting ActivateDecision (architecturally preferable) with UpdateDecision(status='effective').

anchor: Action API: RequestAction, GetAction, CancelAction (potentially RetryAction if well-defined). No direct POST /execute — RequestAction → Authorization → Execution.
statement: Defines the Action API and warns strongly against a direct execution endpoint that would collapse Request and Execution.

anchor: EvaluateActionAuthorization(actionId,principal,scope,context) → AuthorizationResult{authorizationId,decision,conditions,validity}. Authorization ≠ Boolean.
statement: Defines the Authorization API, requiring it to be independently auditable (Authorization->Policy->Decision, and potentially Authorization->Context) and to support conditional results (e.g. ALLOW condition:stagingOnly, or ALLOW condition:humanApprovalRequiredForProduction).

anchor: CanExecute checks Authorization valid, Context valid, Required verification passed, Subject available, Action still unchanged. ActionFingerprint = Hash(ActionDefinition). AuthorizedAction ≠ ModifiedAction.
statement: Extends the execution gate with an 'action still unchanged' predicate and introduces ActionFingerprint (a hash binding authorization to exact action parameters) and ContextFingerprint (binding authorization to the exact evaluated context), with the high-risk-action rule that authorization must bind to Action+Context+Scope; worked example of the danger without binding — authorizing 'upgrade Nexus in staging' but executing 'upgrade Nexus in production.'

anchor: CI/CD requests GetApplicableRules, RunVerification, RegisterEvidence, GetFindings — Agent and CI/CD become symmetric consumers of Governed APIs. KnowledgeOS should not become an 'AI-only' system.
statement: Positions CI/CD as another important consumer participating in the same assurance model as agents, on equal footing.

anchor: KnowledgeOS → Engineering Port → {Nexus Adapter, Git Adapter, Kubernetes Adapter, CI Adapter}. NexusPort{getCurrentState(),getRepositories(),getBlobStores(),executeReadOperation()}. Domain → Nexus REST DTO is forbidden; Domain → Port → Adapter → Nexus DTO required.
statement: Defines the engineering-adapter port pattern and a worked NexusPort contract, translating ExternalModel->KnowledgeOSContract in both directions (NexusResponse->Observation and KnowledgeOSAction->NexusCommand), explicitly forbidding direct domain-to-external-DTO leakage.

anchor: Authentication + Authorization + Scope + Audit. Principal (Human/Agent/Service/CI-CD/System) ≠ requestedBy.
statement: Requires every external API request to have an identifiable principal beyond a mere 'requestedBy' field, and full authentication+authorization+scope+audit, not authentication alone.

anchor: Principal=Codex, DelegatedBy=HumanUser. An agent cannot acquire more authority through delegation than the delegating principal possesses. Authority_agent ⊆ Authority_delegator.
statement: Defines the delegation model (Principal + DelegatedBy making the authority chain explicit) and its governing invariant, subject to policy.

anchor: RequestID, Principal, TraceID, Timestamp, Operation for every material API interaction — part of the evidence/provenance chain. IdempotencyKey for retried commands (e.g. ActivateDecision, RegisterEvidence).
statement: Requires API-level audit fields and idempotency keys, worked with a network-failure-after-commit retry example showing why idempotency matters.

anchor: CONTEXT_EXPIRED, AUTHORIZATION_DENIED, RULE_NOT_APPLICABLE, EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, ACTION_ALREADY_EXECUTED, INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION — not '500 Something went wrong.'
statement: Defines a semantic API error model; requires explicit API versioning applied at the contract level (not an excuse for uncontrolled breaking changes), preferring backward-compatible additions with breaking semantic changes requiring a new contract version.

anchor: Driving Adapters (API/Agent/CI) → Application Core (Commands/Queries) → Domain Model (Aggregates/Rules) → Ports → {Database, Graph, External APIs}.
statement: Presents the complete hexagonal API-boundary architecture diagram, and separates the layer responsibilities: API translates, Application orchestrates, Domain protects invariants, Infrastructure integrates — 'a natural continuation of the previously frozen hexagonal architecture principles.'

anchor: Capability Contract, not CRUD Contract. AuthorizeAction(42) vs PATCH /actions/42{status:AUTHORIZED}. ExecuteVerification(ruleId,subject) vs POST /verification{status:PASS}. RegisterEvidence+VerifyClaim vs POST /claims{verified:true}.
statement: States the stable interface principle is Capability Contract over CRUD Contract, with three worked weak/strong pairs (authorization, verification, evidence) each showing the strong form forces the system to execute the actual domain semantics rather than accept a caller-supplied result.

anchor: Agent ↛ SetClaimVerified(true). Agent → RequestVerification → DeterministicChecker → Verification. This is the anti-hallucination architecture.
statement: Names the API design pattern the 'anti-hallucination architecture' — the platform structurally prevents an agent from manufacturing authoritative state by requiring verification to be produced through a deterministic checker rather than supplied directly.

anchor: Agent assertion (LOW) → Candidate knowledge → Evidence → Deterministic verification → Governed state (HIGH). API design = Governance enforcement boundary.
statement: States the API trust hierarchy and concludes API design is not merely technical interface design but determines which state transitions are structurally possible — 'API design = Governance enforcement boundary.'

anchor: Minimal KnowledgeOS v1 API: GetGovernedContext; RequestVerification/GetVerification; RegisterEvidence/GetEvidence; CreateTask/CreateRecommendation; RequestAction/GetAction; EvaluateAuthorization; ExecuteAuthorizedAction/GetExecution. GoldenTrace → MinimalContracts → ReferenceImplementation, then expand.
statement: Defines the minimum API surface needed for the first Golden Trace across six capability domains, explicitly rejecting building '150 endpoints before the first vertical slice works'; requires the same call sequence to work identically for Claude and Codex (Claude/Codex compatibility test) without changing governance/rules/evidence/authorization/domain semantics — only the agent adapter differs.

anchor: API-001: External consumers cannot directly mutate authoritative domain state. ... API-008: Graph and search projections are not authoritative mutation interfaces.
statement: Defines eight API-level architecture invariants API-001..008: no direct external mutation of domain state; verification verdicts produced by assurance not supplied by caller; material actions cannot bypass authorization; every material operation has trace/correlation identity; external system models do not cross the port/adapter boundary; agent capability does not imply execution authority; authoritative state transitions occur through explicit domain operations; graph/search projections are not authoritative mutation interfaces (preventing clients from treating the graph as master state).

anchor: Agents consume governed capabilities; they do not manipulate KnowledgeOS state directly. The first API does not need to be large. It needs to be semantically correct.
statement: Step 148 verdict: the crucial boundary the API architecture establishes, and the conclusion that the Golden Trace gives the minimum contract set required for the first real KnowledgeOS vertical slice.

anchor: Transactional State, Evidence, Graph, Search, Event History, Agent Memory — avoid one database for everything; polyglot persistence with one authoritative transactional model per bounded context.
statement: Opens Step 149 (Persistence & Data Architecture): poses where state lives and which storage mechanism is authoritative for which information kind, targeting a polyglot persistence boundary rather than one universal database.

anchor: The Gītā is an external conceptual lens for testing KnowledgeOS—not a new 'Gītā dimension' of the architecture. ARCHITECTURE: CONCEPTUALLY VALIDATED but NOT YET COMPLETE.
statement: States the governing methodological rule for using Chapter 4 as a stress test (separating what the text says from architectural inference) and the executive verdict: Chapter 4 does not invalidate Steps 1-155 but exposes a significant missing kernel capability — knowledge lineage and epistemic provenance as first-class architectural concepts, to be addressed before Step 156.

anchor: Knowledge ≠ Document. Knowledge = Content + Lineage + Authority + Transmission + Context.
statement: Derives from the chapter's description of a broken succession (Kṛṣṇa->Vivasvān->Manu->Ikṣvāku) that knowledge is not reducible to a document but a composite of content, lineage, authority, transmission, and context.

anchor: KnowledgeRelationship = (Knower, Knowing, Known). KnowledgeArtifact, KnowledgeSource, KnowledgeAuthority, KnowledgeRecipient, KnowledgeTransmission, KnowledgeInterpretation, KnowledgeContext.
statement: Strengthens the pre-existing Knower≠Known / KnowledgeRelationship=(Knower,Knowing,Known) model (established in earlier batches) using Arjuna's reception of the teaching as an example that the recipient's relationship to the source matters, not merely content copying; concludes KnowledgeOS should preserve seven named sub-concepts rather than reducing to Document->Chunk->Embedding.

anchor: K_{i+1} = T_i(K_i) + epsilon_i. D(K_i,K_0) = distance(CurrentKnowledge, AuthoritativeKnowledge).
statement: States 'the most important discovery' — knowledge can degrade in transmission without the source itself changing (KnowledgeState_t ≠ SourceState) — and formalizes a transmission-chain model K0->K1->...->Kn with per-step error epsilon_i, and a knowledge-drift divergence measure D(Ki,K0), with three qualitative regimes (D≈0 faithful, D increasing interpretation/drift, D beyond threshold governance intervention); explicitly disclaims any claim of statistically determining spiritual truth — the engineering conclusion is only that KnowledgeOS needs mechanisms to detect provenance loss, semantic drift and divergence from an authoritative version.

anchor: ArchitectureRule { source, authority, version, derivedFrom, interpretedBy, effectiveFrom }. DeclaredArchitecture + Authority + Lineage.
statement: Extends the existing Architecture Registry's DeclaredArchitecture dimension with authority and lineage fields, so the registry answers not only 'what is the rule' but 'where did this rule come from' and 'who had authority to establish it.'

anchor: Authority precedes governance validity.
statement: States Chapter 4's emphasis on authorized succession (and warning against independently manufactured process) validates the existing Governance Runtime chain (Proposal->Decision->Implementation->Verification / Governance->Declared Rule->Implementation->Assurance).

anchor: AuthorityChain: Authoritative Source → Authority → Decision → Rule → Derived Rule → Implementation → Verification. Generic 'KnowledgeAuthority' or 'AuthorityReference,' not 'GitaAuthority.'
statement: Proposes a missing generic AuthorityChain concept (explicitly generalized, not named after the religious source), extending the existing Decision->ArchitectureVersion model.

anchor: Restoration ≠ Modification. Restore(K) ≠ CreateNewTruth(K).
statement: Uses the chapter's account of an ancient teaching being re-spoken after the lineage was lost to derive a restoration-vs-modification distinction, mapped onto the immutable-version model (Knowledge v1 -> Transmission -> Drift/loss -> Restoration -> Validated representation).

anchor: Same underlying principle → different contextual expression. Context = f(Subject,Task,Role,Authority,Scope).
statement: Strengthens the existing Context model using the chapter's '2+2=4 at different mathematical levels' analogy: KnowledgeOS must distinguish a Canonical Principle from multiple Contextual Interpretations without treating each as a new canonical principle.

anchor: Source → LLM → New 'knowledge' (dangerous) vs Authoritative Knowledge → Context Construction → AI Interpretation → Derived Statement → Provenance → Verification (correct). AI output must retain epistemic lineage.
statement: Applies the contextual-re-expression finding to AI specifically: contrasts the dangerous architecture where an LLM's interpretation becomes 'new knowledge' with provenance lost, against the correct model retaining lineage through to verification.

anchor: AI must not silently convert inference into authoritative knowledge.
statement: States Chapter 4's repeated distinction between authoritative transmission and speculative interpretation reinforces (via an independently-derived route) the anti-hallucination invariant against silently converting inference into authority.

anchor: G_K=(V,E) with nodes {Source,Knowledge,Interpretation,Derivation,Decision,Observation,Verification} and edges {derivedFrom,transmittedBy,interpretedBy,approvedBy,verifiedBy,supersedes,contextualizes}. A KnowledgeOS statement is x + Path(x).
statement: Models knowledge lineage as a directed graph, concluding a KnowledgeOS statement must carry its epistemic path, not just its value; gives a corresponding KnowledgeClaim schema (claimId, proposition, source, authority, provenance, context, derivation, version, validity, evidence).

anchor: Authority → Hearing → Inquiry → Understanding → Knowledge → Action. Source → Context → Inquiry → Evidence → Interpretation → Verification.
